message.reasoning_content:
Analyze kernel semantics and record update.

Key analysis: kernel keeps order mapping. Define order[i]: logical row i located at physical row order[i]? Let's check.

_reorder: next[row] = order[perm[row]]. Semantics: logical C_next = C_current[P]. Logical row i of C_next = logical row P[i] of C_current. Logical row i lives at physical order[i] (before), and after, next_order[i] = order[P[i]]. Correct.

_append: Cache[physical r] += Delta[source = order[row]]. So physical row r gets Delta[order[r]] added. Logical row i is physical order[i], gets Delta[order[i]]. But contract: Delta addresses current logical rows, i.e. logical row i should get Delta[i]. So the kernel adds Delta indexed by physical location — bug unless order[i] == i. Actually wait: which mapping is order? Let's re-derive _materialize: Output[logical row r] = Cache[physical = order[r]]. So logical r ← physical order[r]. Consistent: order[logical]=physical.

_append: at physical row r, adds Delta[order[r]] — Delta indexed by physical. Should add Delta[r] since logical row r resides at physical order[r], so physical order[r] += Delta[r]. Bug: adds Delta indexed by physical address instead of logical.

Wait check smoke word (0,2): after op0, order[i]=P0[i]. Then append: physical r += Delta[order[r]]. Logical output row i = physical order[i] += Delta[order[order[i]]]. Reference: logical row i = old logical P0[i] + Delta[i]. Hmm. After op0, logical row i = C[P0[i]], located at physical order[i]=P0[i]? Wait initially order[i]=i, logical i = physical i. After op0, next_order[i] = order[P0[i]] = P0[i]. Logical row i = old logical row P0[i] = C[P0[i]], at physical P0[i]. Correct. Append: physical r += Delta[order[r]] = Delta[P0[r]]. Logical i at physical P0[i] += Delta[P0[P0[i]]] = Delta[i] since P0 is involution! That's why smoke passes — involution property hides it. Compositions like op0 then op1: order[i]=P1[P0[i]], physical r gets Delta[order[r]]; logical i at physical order[i] gets Delta[order[order[i]]] which equals Delta[i] only if order∘order = id, which needs P0P1P0P1 = id — not guaranteed. Also op0,2: order after op0 is P0 (involution), so passes; that's why (0,2) passed. But (0,1,2)? order = P1∘P0... wait next_order[i]=order[P[i]]: after op0 order=P0; after op1 order[i]=P0[P1[i]] = P0∘P1. Not necessarily involution. So words like (0,1,2), (1,0,2) likely fail. Risk: append indexing bug masked by involution in smoke tests.

Also words ending without 2, empty word, length 3-4 reorders: fine since reorder is correct. Also multiple 2s: second append adds Delta again but same wrong indexing... always Delta indexed by physical each time; contract says each op2 adds Delta to current logical rows, so logical i gets Delta[i] each time; kernel gives logical i Delta[order^{-1}... anyway.

Record update.
